newsitem.title: CROATIA: U.N. says Serbs disenfranchised in Croatia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says Serbs disenfranchised in Croatia.

text.p: The United Nations said on Tuesday it was disappointed the Croatian government had not made it possible for all citizens in the last Serb enclave in Croatia to vote in Sunday's presidential election.
The criticism came on the heels of a report by an international monitoring mission which said the elections had been free but not fair because of a biased election campaign.

The region of Eastern Slavonia is currently administered by the U.N. but is due to revert to Croatian government control next month. Residents were registered in April for municipal elections but voters' lists were found to be incomplete on the day of the poll.
The government was supposed to provide updated lists before Sunday's presidential election to allow everyone to vote.
President Franjo Tudjman won a second five-year term of office in the election.
The U.N. said it was unfortunate that the Croatian Ministry of Administration was unable to "follow through on their commitment to update the voter lists".
It said the lists contained "several thousand names less than on the lists adjusted during the April election".

It said the U.N. Transitional Authority in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) "is deeply disappointed that elements of the Croatian government were unable to fulfil their obligation to ensure that all Croatian citizens in the UNTAES region, wishing to vote, could not do so in their presidential elections."
